md_name: Herbicide Compound Characterization and Bioactivity Screening
md_description: This workflow covers laboratory synthesis and purification of candidate herbicide compounds, their structural and physicochemical characterization by NMR and mass spectrometry, and in vitro screening against plant enzymes and cellular pathways. The pipeline produces raw spectral signals, assay readouts, and downstream derived metrics for potency, selectivity, and potential toxicity to support agricultural candidate evaluation.

starting_reagents.reasoning: The starting_reagents node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic identity and origin fields for the chemical precursors themselves: reagent identity, supplier/catalog identifiers, lot/batch, purity, form, and storage/source provenance. I excluded any synthesis parameters, reaction conditions, purification details, characterization settings, assay information, or derived outputs because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there was no need to suppress overlaps with existing schema fields. I also avoided experiment-wide identifiers since those are typically defined once at the root entity level, not repeated for reagent-level entities.

md_schema.descr: Chemical name or common name of the starting material used as a precursor for herbicide synthesis; record the supplier label used in the lab notebook, e.g. '2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid' or an internal inventory name.
Optional hashed chemical identity identifier for the starting reagent; use the standard 27-character InChIKey format when available to support unambiguous matching across datasets.
Vendor or source organization that provided the starting reagent; capture the supplier name as listed on the certificate of analysis or purchase order.
Supplier catalog or product number for the starting reagent; useful for exact procurement traceability, e.g. 'ABC-12345'.
Manufacturer or vendor lot/batch identifier for the reagent container used in this synthesis workflow; record exactly as printed on the label or COA.
Purity of the starting reagent before use in synthesis, expressed as percent by vendor certificate or in-house QC at the time of receipt; typical range 0-100, e.g. 98.5.
Physical form of the starting material as received and stored before synthesis; choose the best match for handling and preparation.

Storage condition for the starting reagent prior to use in synthesis, describing how the precursor was kept in inventory; use a concise lab-standard description such as '4 C desiccated' or '-20 C under nitrogen'.
Origin category of the starting reagent before synthesis; indicates whether the precursor was commercially purchased, custom synthesized, or isolated from another internal workflow.

synthesis_process.reasoning: The synthesis_process node is a Process, so I included only synthesis operation details: reaction protocol, key reagents/stoichiometry, conditions, duration, atmosphere, catalyst/solvent context, and a process-level yield/quality indicator. I excluded intrinsic properties of the starting reagents and any properties of the crude product itself, since those belong to upstream Entity and downstream Entity nodes respectively. I also excluded purification, characterization, assay, and computational analysis fields because they are outside the synthesis operation. No already_generated fields were supplied for this step, so no overlap suppression was needed.

md_schema.descr: Primary synthesis transformation used to convert starting reagents into crude herbicide candidates; describe the named reaction class or route followed in this workflow, e.g. coupling, substitution, alkylation, or condensation.
Reaction scale for the synthesis step, measured at the point of execution as the nominal amount of limiting reagent used per batch; typical range 0.001-1000 mmol, e.g. 5.0 mmol.
Solvent or mixed-solvent system used during synthesis; record the main reaction medium present at the time the transformation was carried out, e.g. 'THF/water' or 'dichloromethane'.
Key catalyst, reagent, or activating system used to drive the synthesis reaction, excluding the starting reagents themselves; record the operationally important chemical system used in the process.
Temperature of the reaction mixture during synthesis, measured during the transformation step; typical range -100 to 250 Celsius, e.g. 25.0.
Elapsed time for the synthesis reaction or main transformation stage, measured from initiation to quench/workup; typical range 1-10080 minutes, e.g. 120.0.
Atmospheric or environmental control used during synthesis, describing whether the reaction was run under air, inert gas, or another controlled atmosphere.
Brief description of the post-reaction workup used immediately after synthesis before crude isolation, e.g. aqueous quench, extraction, filtration, or concentration.

Yield of crude herbicide candidate material obtained after the synthesis step and initial isolation, expressed as percent of theoretical maximum; record as the process-level output quality indicator, typical range 0-100.

crude_compounds.reasoning: The crude_compounds node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the unpurified synthesized material and omitted synthesis conditions, purification parameters, instrument settings, raw data file properties, and downstream analytical results. For this entity, the most useful fields describe what the crude material is, how much of it exists, its physical appearance, composition/purity state, and traceability to the synthesis batch. No already_generated fields were provided, and I avoided repeating root-level experiment identifiers or fields better suited to the synthesis_process node.

md_schema.descr: Internal identifier assigned to the crude herbicide candidate material after synthesis and before purification; use a stable string identifier such as 'CRUDE_001' or the lab's batch label.
Identifier linking this crude material back to the synthesis batch that produced it; use the exact batch or reaction identifier recorded at synthesis completion.
Mass of the isolated crude material obtained after synthesis and initial solvent removal, measured at the point of crude collection before purification; typical range 0-100000 mg, e.g. 250.4 mg.
Observed physical appearance of the crude material at the time of collection before purification, such as oil, foam, gum, solid, or residue.
Free-text description of the crude material state and handling condition before purification, including color, homogeneity, or notable contaminants seen by the operator.
Approximate purity of the crude material before purification, estimated by in-process analysis or operator assessment; typical range 0-100, e.g. 72.5.
Whether the crude material is believed to still contain residual reaction solvent or volatiles at the time of transfer to purification.
Short description of how the crude material was held between synthesis completion and purification, e.g. 'room temperature under nitrogen' or '4 C desiccated'.

purification_process.reasoning: The purification_process node is a Process, so I included only the operational details of how crude compounds were purified and isolated to yield assay- and instrument-ready material. I captured the purification strategy, media/method, key mobile-phase or elution conditions, step count, duration, recovery, and a process-level purity/quality outcome. I excluded any intrinsic properties of the crude or purified compounds themselves, because those belong on the input/output Entity nodes, and I did not include characterization or assay fields because those are downstream. No already_generated fields were supplied here, so there was no overlap to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Primary purification strategy used to isolate herbicide candidates from crude reaction mixtures; record the method actually executed, e.g. flash chromatography, preparative HPLC, recrystallization, or extraction.
Stationary phase or purification medium used during the purification step, if applicable; describe the resin or sorbent loaded into the separation system, e.g. silica gel, C18, alumina, or other.
Solvent or mobile-phase system used to elute and isolate the purified compounds during the purification process; record the actual solvent mixture or gradient system used at the time of separation.
Number of sequential purification passes or rounds required to obtain the final isolated herbicide candidate material; typical range 1-10, e.g. 2.
Elapsed time spent performing the purification and isolation step, measured from loading the crude material to collection of the purified fractions; typical range 1-10080 minutes, e.g. 90.
Percentage of crude material recovered as purified compound after purification, measured at process completion relative to the crude input mass; typical range 0-100, e.g. 35.2.

Estimated purity of the isolated compound at the end of the purification process, measured by the process-quality assessment immediately after isolation and before downstream characterization; typical range 0-100, e.g. 96.8.
Whether multiple collected fractions or subfractions were combined to form the final isolated material during purification.
Concise free-text notes on purification-specific issues observed during isolation, such as emulsion formation, co-elution, or fraction losses.

purified_compounds.reasoning: I corrected the purified_compounds schema to remove the colliding field name storage_condition, which had already been generated earlier in the DAG. I kept the other entity-level fields that describe the purified material itself and its readiness for downstream use, while still excluding purification, capture, assay, and derivative content that belongs elsewhere in the workflow. Because the user only flagged a field-name collision, I minimally revised the node schema rather than changing the node's semantic scope.

md_schema.descr: Internal identifier assigned to the isolated herbicide candidate compound after purification; use a stable string such as 'PUR_001' or the laboratory inventory label.
Identifier of the crude compound batch from which this purified material was isolated; record the exact upstream crude batch or reaction identifier.
Mass of isolated purified compound available after completion of purification, measured at the point of final collection and drying; typical range 0-100000 mg, e.g. 12.5 mg.
Physical state of the purified compound at the time it is prepared for characterization or assay, such as solid, oil, powder, crystalline, or lyophilized material.
Storage condition for the purified compound before characterization or bioactivity testing, e.g. '-20 C desiccated', '4 C in amber vial', or 'under inert gas'.
Whether a dedicated aliquot of the purified compound was prepared specifically for structural characterization or bioactivity assays.
Operational status indicating whether the purified compound was considered ready for downstream NMR, mass spectrometry, or assay workflows at the time of handoff.
Brief free-text description of the purified material's observed appearance after isolation and drying, such as color or crystallinity.

nmr_capture.reasoning: The nmr_capture node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration for the NMR acquisition: instrument identity, field strength, nucleus measured, pulse/acquisition settings, sample temperature, and run/session metadata. I excluded purified compound properties, spectral file properties, and downstream interpretation outputs because those belong to the Entity, Signal, and Derivative nodes respectively. I also avoided the previously generated field storage_condition due to the reported DAG-wide collision, and I did not repeat any assay or synthesis fields that are outside the capture territory. No additional already_generated fields were supplied in this prompt.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the NMR spectrometer used for this capture session; record the hardware vendor responsible for the instrument body.
Model designation of the NMR spectrometer used for this capture session; use the exact instrument model string from the device label or service record, e.g. 'Avance III HD'.
Serial number of the NMR spectrometer used for this capture session; capture the instrument's unique hardware serial exactly as recorded in the facility inventory.
Nominal magnetic field strength of the NMR instrument, measured as the proton frequency in MHz for the configured spectrometer; typical range 100-1200 MHz, e.g. 400.0.
Nuclear isotope acquired during the NMR capture session; record the observed nucleus for the raw spectra being generated.
NMR pulse sequence used for this capture session, as selected by the operator for data acquisition; record the exact sequence name or shorthand, e.g. 'zg30' or 'hsqcetgp'.
Number of transients accumulated during the NMR acquisition session for the sample; typical range 1-100000, e.g. 16.
Receiver gain setting used on the NMR instrument during this capture session; record the configured gain value as set before acquisition.
Temperature of the sample during NMR acquisition, measured or set at the instrument during the capture session; typical range -150 to 150 Celsius, e.g. 25.0.
Internal identifier for the NMR acquisition session corresponding to one run or method execution; use a stable string such as 'NMR_RUN_001'.
Date on which the NMR capture session was performed; record the acquisition day in ISO date format (YYYY-MM-DD).

nmr_spectra.reasoning: The nmr_spectra node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artefact properties: file format, file size, dimensionality, spectral range, resolution-related technical parameters, acquisition linkage, storage location, and basic technical quality indicators. I excluded instrument settings and sample properties because those belong to the nmr_capture and purified_compounds nodes respectively, and I excluded any interpretation, identity calls, or structural annotations because those belong to downstream Derivative nodes. I also avoided the previously generated storage_condition field due to the reported DAG-wide collision and did not repeat any capture-session fields beyond a necessary foreign-key style link to the acquisition session.

md_schema.descr: Filename or object name of the raw NMR spectral file as stored immediately after acquisition; use the exact instrument-exported name when available, e.g. 'sample1.fid' or 'run_04.dx'.

Raw file format of the NMR signal artifact, describing the technical encoding used by the spectrometer export or converted archive; record the on-disk format, e.g. fid, JCAMP-DX, or vendor-native binary.
Size of the raw NMR spectral file in bytes at the time of storage or export; typical range 1-1000000000000, e.g. 2456789.
Number of acquired dimensions in the raw NMR dataset, measured from the signal file structure; use 1 for standard 1D spectra or higher values for multidimensional experiments.
Total spectral width recorded in the raw NMR acquisition, expressed in Hertz and measured as the full frequency span covered by the signal artifact; typical range 1-10000000 Hz, e.g. 8000.0.
Number of data points stored per spectrum or per indirect dimension in the raw NMR file; record the acquired digital resolution at the signal level, typical range 1-10000000, e.g. 65536.
Identifier linking the raw spectra file back to the NMR capture session that generated it; use the exact session identifier or run label assigned during acquisition.
File system path, object-store URI, or repository location where the raw NMR spectral artifact is stored; record the technical storage location only, not sample storage.
Basic technical quality metric for the raw NMR spectrum, calculated from the signal artifact itself or from acquisition QC at file creation; typical range 0-10000, e.g. 125.4.
Whether the raw NMR spectrum passed a basic baseline stability check at the signal level immediately after acquisition or export.

ms_capture.reasoning: The ms_capture node is a Capture, so I kept only acquisition-session and instrument-configuration fields for the mass spectrometry run. I preserved the hardware, ionization, scan, analyzer, scan-range, collision-energy, and session-link fields, but removed acquisition_date because it was reported as already generated elsewhere in the DAG. I also continued to exclude sample properties, raw file metadata, and derivative outputs, since those belong to other node types. No additional already_generated list was provided in this prompt, so the only explicit collision I had to resolve was acquisition_date.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the mass spectrometer used for this capture session; record the hardware vendor responsible for the instrument body.
Model designation of the mass spectrometer used for this capture session; use the exact model string from the instrument label or service record, e.g. 'Q Exactive Plus' or 'Triple Quad 6500'.
Serial number of the mass spectrometer used for this capture session; capture the unique hardware serial exactly as recorded in facility inventory.
Ionization polarity or mode used during the MS acquisition, describing how ions were generated for the raw spectra; choose the setting used at the instrument for the sample run.
Type of ion source configured on the mass spectrometer for this capture session, e.g. ESI, APCI, MALDI, or EI.
Acquisition scan type or experiment mode used during the MS session, e.g. full scan, product ion scan, or SIM; record the actual acquisition mode selected for the sample.
Mass analyzer configured for the instrument during this capture session, such as orbitrap, quadrupole, time-of-flight, or ion trap.
m/z range acquired during the MS session, measured as the lower-to-upper scan window configured on the instrument; typical range 1-100000 m/z, e.g. '50-1500'.
Collision energy setting used for tandem MS or fragmentation-related acquisition during this capture session, if applicable; typical range 0-200 eV, e.g. 30.0.
Internal identifier for the MS acquisition session corresponding to one run or method execution; use a stable string such as 'MS_RUN_001'.

ms_spectra.reasoning: The ms_spectra node is a Signal, so I kept only raw data artifact metadata: file identity, format, size, dimensionality, scan/m/z coverage, provenance link to the capture session, storage location, and a technical quality flag. I removed signal_to_noise_ratio because it was already generated earlier in the DAG and cannot be repeated. I continued to exclude capture settings, sample properties, and any downstream interpretation fields because they belong to other node types.

md_schema.descr: Filename or object name of the raw mass spectral file as stored immediately after acquisition; use the exact export name when available, e.g. 'sample1.raw' or 'run_04.mzML'.

Raw file format of the mass spectrum artifact, describing the technical encoding used by the instrument export or converted archive; record the on-disk format, e.g. mzML, mzXML, vendor-native binary, or text export.
Size of the raw mass spectral file in bytes at the time of storage or export; typical range 1-1000000000000, e.g. 8456123.

Number of acquired dimensions or channels in the raw MS dataset, measured from the signal file structure; use 1 for a standard single-spectrum acquisition or higher values for multidimensional MS data.
Number of scans or spectra contained in the raw MS file, measured from the signal artifact itself; typical range 1-10000000, e.g. 128.
Observed m/z span present in the raw MS artifact, recorded as the minimum-to-maximum values represented in the stored signal file; typical range 1-100000 m/z, e.g. '50-1500'.
Identifier linking the raw mass spectra file back to the MS capture session that generated it; use the exact session identifier or run label assigned during acquisition.
File system path, object-store URI, or repository location where the raw MS spectral artifact is stored; record only the technical storage location, not sample storage.
Whether the stored MS file is centroided rather than profile data at the signal level immediately after acquisition or conversion.

nmr_interpretation.reasoning: The nmr_interpretation node is a Process, so I included only the computational interpretation operation details: software identity, version, repository, input linkage, key processing parameters, and an interpretation quality indicator. I excluded raw spectral file properties, capture settings, and the derived identity outputs themselves because those belong to the Signal, Capture, and Derivative nodes respectively. I also avoided previously generated field names that have caused DAG-wide collisions, especially signal_to_noise_ratio and acquisition_date, and kept the schema strictly about how the interpretation was performed.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or computational package used to interpret the raw NMR spectra into structural features; record the exact tool name used in this process, e.g. 'MestReNova' or 'ACD/NMR Processor'.
Version of the NMR interpretation software used for this process step; capture the exact release string or build number, e.g. '14.2.0'.
Source repository, package registry, or vendor distribution from which the NMR interpretation software was obtained; record the canonical code or vendor source when available.
Identifier of the raw NMR spectra or acquisition session supplied as input to this interpretation process; use the exact upstream signal or session identifier for traceability.
Peak picking or signal feature extraction method applied during NMR interpretation; record the algorithm or rule set used to identify spectral features.
Reference standard or calibration compound used during interpretation to align chemical shifts, if applicable; record the standard employed for the processed spectra.
Mass/chemical shift tolerance used by the interpretation workflow when matching or annotating NMR features, measured in ppm; typical range 0-10 ppm, e.g. 0.02.

Process-level confidence or quality score indicating how well the NMR interpretation step resolved structural features from the raw spectra; typically scaled 0-1 or 0-100 depending on software, record the numeric value used in this workflow.
Strategy used to annotate interpreted NMR features, such as manual assignment, semi-automated assignment, or automated library matching.

nmr_identity.reasoning: The nmr_identity node is a Derivative, so I included only computed structural evidence and output-quality fields derived from the interpreted NMR results: assigned structure labels, confidence, matched motifs, diagnostic peaks, and derived annotation summary. I excluded raw spectra properties, capture settings, and interpretation workflow parameters because those belong to the Signal, Capture, and Process nodes respectively. I also avoided previously generated field names that were known to collide across the DAG, especially signal_to_noise_ratio and acquisition_date, and kept the schema focused on the scientific result rather than the computation method.

md_schema.descr: Computed or assigned chemical structure name for the herbicide candidate supported by NMR evidence; record the best-supported structural label produced by the derivative step.

Confidence score indicating how strongly the NMR-derived features support the assigned molecular identity; typically a numeric score in the 0-1 or 0-100 range, record the value emitted by this derivative workflow.
Summary of the most informative NMR peaks or resonances used to support the structural identity call, reported as a concise derived annotation rather than a raw peak table.
Functional groups or structural motifs inferred from the NMR analysis as part of the derived identity evidence; report the consensus assignments made by the workflow.
Free-text or compact structured summary of the molecular identity supported by the NMR derivative, including any unresolved ambiguities or alternative assignments.
Overall derivative status for the NMR identity call, indicating whether the spectra support a confident assignment or remain ambiguous.

ms_interpretation.reasoning: The ms_interpretation node is a Process, so I kept only process-oriented computation settings and excluded raw data, output descriptors, and any previously generated field names. In response to the collision report, I removed interpretation_confidence_score and retained only unique MS interpretation parameters: software identity, repository, input linkage, calibration, detection, and tolerance settings. This preserves the node's semantic territory while avoiding duplication across the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or computational package used to interpret the raw mass spectra into molecular-weight and property features; record the exact tool name used in this process, e.g. 'MassLynx' or 'MS-DIAL'.
Version of the MS interpretation software used for this process step; capture the exact release string or build number, e.g. '4.3' or '2.90'.
Source repository, package registry, or vendor distribution from which the MS interpretation software was obtained; record the canonical code or vendor source when available.
Identifier of the raw mass spectra or acquisition session supplied as input to this interpretation process; use the exact upstream signal or session identifier for traceability.
Calibration approach applied before or during interpretation of the mass spectra, such as internal calibration, lock-mass correction, or external calibration.
Threshold used by the interpretation workflow to detect peaks or features in the raw mass spectra; record the numerical cutoff in the units used by the software, typically intensity or signal units.
Method used to collapse isotopic envelopes into monoisotopic features during interpretation of the mass spectra; record the algorithm or rule applied by the workflow.
Mass accuracy tolerance used during interpretation when matching observed m/z values to inferred molecular features, measured in parts per million; typical range 0-100 ppm, e.g. 5.0.

ms_properties.reasoning: The ms_properties node is a Derivative, so I included only computed molecular-property outputs inferred from MS: monoisotopic mass, formula assignment, adduct/charge state, mass error, isotope pattern fit, and a derivative-level confidence/quality flag. I excluded raw spectrum properties, capture settings, and interpretation workflow parameters because those belong to the Signal, Capture, and Process nodes respectively. I also avoided the previously generated collision-prone field interpretation_confidence_score and focused on the scientific result of the MS-derived computation, not the method used to produce it.

md_schema.descr: Computed monoisotopic mass assigned to the herbicide candidate from MS interpretation, expressed in Daltons; record the derived value reported by the workflow, typical range 1-10000 Da, e.g. 312.1456.
Best-supported molecular formula inferred from the mass spectral data; record the derived elemental composition string, e.g. 'C15H12Cl2N2O3'.
Adduct or ion state assigned to the detected molecular species in the derived MS output, e.g. [M+H]+ or [M-H]-; report the final interpreted ion form.
Difference between observed and theoretical m/z for the assigned species, expressed in parts per million; typical range -1000 to 1000 ppm, e.g. 2.3.

Derived score describing how well the observed isotope envelope matches the predicted isotopic pattern for the assigned molecular species; typical range 0-1 or 0-100 depending on workflow, record the numeric value used.
Compact summary of the MS-derived physicochemical features assigned to the compound, including any notable fragmentation- or adduct-based evidence used in the final property call.

Overall confidence in the derived MS property assignment, reflecting how strongly the mass spectrum supports the predicted mass and formula; typical range 0-1 or 0-100 depending on workflow, record the value produced by the derivative step.
Overall status of the MS-derived property call, indicating whether the assigned properties are confident, partial, ambiguous, or rejected.

assay_cell_material.reasoning: The assay_cell_material node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic biological properties and provenance of the plant assay targets: species, tissue/cell type, enzyme/pathway identity, preparation state, origin, passage/culture history, and viability/activity status. I excluded assay protocol details, capture platform settings, and readout files because those belong to the bioactivity assay Capture and Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating compound identifiers or downstream response metrics, since this node describes the biological target material itself, not the screening operation. No already_generated fields were supplied here, so there was no overlap suppression needed.

md_schema.descr: Internal identifier for the plant assay material or biological target preparation used in screening; use a stable lab identifier such as 'PLANT_ASSAY_01'.
Plant species or taxon from which the enzyme preparation or cellular assay system was derived; record the organism used as the biological target, e.g. 'Arabidopsis thaliana' or another plant species.
Tissue, cell type, or preparation type used for the assay target material, such as leaf tissue, root tissue, suspension cells, microsomes, or enzyme extract.
Primary plant enzyme, pathway, or cellular process represented by this assay material for herbicide screening, e.g. photosynthesis, amino acid biosynthesis, or cell wall formation.
Preparation state of the assay target material at the time it is placed into the screening workflow, such as fresh, frozen, lysate, purified enzyme, or cultured cells.
Origin of the plant assay material, such as greenhouse-grown, field-collected, purchased culture, or in-house propagated source material.
Date on which the assay target material was prepared or harvested before use in the bioactivity screening workflow; record the calendar date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD).
Current status of the assay target material immediately before screening, indicating whether cells or enzyme preparations were active and suitable for use.
Passage or subculture number for cell-based assay materials, if applicable; record the operational history count at the time of screening preparation, typically an integer >= 0.

bioactivity_assay_capture.reasoning: The bioactivity_assay_capture node is a Capture, so I included only assay-session and instrument-configuration fields: plate reader/workstation identity, assay format, detection channel, incubation, read settings, control layout, and session timing. I excluded properties of the plant assay material, raw readout files, and normalized or derived potency/toxicity metrics because those belong to the Entity, Signal, and Derivative nodes respectively. I also avoided field-name collisions already seen in the DAG, especially storage_condition, acquisition_date, signal_to_noise_ratio, and interpretation_confidence_score. The schema is limited to the settings needed to reproduce the bioactivity acquisition itself.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the automated plate reader or assay workstation used for this capture session; record the hardware vendor responsible for the instrument body.
Model designation of the plate reader or assay workstation used for this capture session; use the exact model string from the device label or service record, e.g. 'Synergy H1' or 'Echo 555'.
Serial number of the assay capture instrument used for this session; capture the unique hardware serial exactly as recorded in facility inventory.
Experimental format used for the bioactivity capture session, describing the physical assay architecture run on the instrument.
Detection channel or assay readout modality configured for the capture session, such as absorbance, fluorescence, luminescence, or impedance.
Incubation temperature used during the assay capture session, measured at the assay workstation or incubator controlling the reaction; typical range 0-50 Celsius, e.g. 25.0.
Incubation time used before the assay readout was captured, measured from compound addition or assay start to measurement; typical range 1-10080 minutes, e.g. 60.0.
Time point at which the assay readout was captured relative to the start of the assay, measured in minutes; typical range 0-10080 minutes, e.g. 30.0.
Whether and how assay controls were laid out on the plate during the capture session, such as positive controls, negative controls, and blanks.
Internal identifier for the bioactivity assay capture session corresponding to one plate run or instrument method execution; use a stable string such as 'ASSAY_RUN_001'.

bioactivity_signal.reasoning: The bioactivity_signal node is a Signal, so I included only raw assay artifact properties: file name, format, size, dimensions, plate/well counts, storage location, acquisition linkage, and basic technical QC. I excluded assay instrument settings and biological target properties because those belong to the bioactivity_assay_capture and assay_cell_material nodes, and I excluded normalized response or potency/toxicity metrics because those belong to downstream derivative nodes. I also avoided previously generated collision-prone field names, especially acquisition_date, storage_condition, signal_to_noise_ratio, and interpretation_confidence_score. The fields here are limited to the raw response data artifact itself.

md_schema.descr: Filename or object name of the raw assay response file as stored immediately after capture; use the exact export name when available, e.g. 'plate01.csv' or 'run_07.txt'.
Raw file format of the assay response artifact, describing the technical encoding used by the capture platform or export pipeline; record the on-disk format, e.g. csv, txt, xlsx, or vendor-native.
Size of the raw assay response file in bytes at the time of storage or export; typical range 1-1000000000000, e.g. 45678.
Number of dimensions represented in the raw assay response file, measured from the signal artifact structure; use 1 for a single response matrix or higher values for multi-parameter readouts.
Total number of wells or reaction positions represented in the raw assay signal artifact; record the effective layout size used in the capture session, e.g. 96, 384, or 1536.
Identifier linking the raw assay response file back to the bioactivity capture session that generated it; use the exact session identifier or run label assigned during acquisition.
File system path, object-store URI, or repository location where the raw assay response artifact is stored; record only the technical storage location, not sample storage.
Measurement scale used in the raw assay response file, such as absorbance units, fluorescence counts, or luminescence counts; record the native scale reported by the instrument/export.
Number of technical replicates represented in the raw assay signal artifact, measured at the file or plate level; typical range 1-1000, e.g. 3.
Basic technical quality flag for the raw assay response file, indicating whether the artifact passed capture-level QC immediately after export.

response_processing.reasoning: The response_processing node is a Process, so I included only computational normalization workflow details: software identity, version, repository, control strategy, normalization method, replicate handling, and a process-level QC indicator. I excluded raw assay response file properties and downstream normalized metrics because those belong to the Signal and Derivative nodes respectively. I also avoided any previously generated collision-prone field names, especially signal_to_noise_ratio, acquisition_date, storage_condition, and interpretation_confidence_score. The schema focuses on how raw assay values were transformed into normalized outputs.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or computational package used to normalize the assay responses; record the exact tool name used in this process, e.g. 'GraphPad Prism' or 'custom normalization script'.
Version of the response normalization software or script used for this process step; capture the exact release string, commit hash, or build number when available.
Source repository, package registry, or vendor distribution from which the response processing software was obtained; record the canonical code or source path when available.
Identifier of the raw assay response session or file supplied as input to this processing step; use the exact upstream signal or session identifier for traceability.
Normalization method applied to raw assay responses, such as percent inhibition against controls, z-score scaling, or baseline subtraction.
Control strategy used for normalization, describing which assay controls anchored the response scaling during processing.
Method used to aggregate technical or biological replicates during response processing, e.g. mean, median, robust fit, or weighted average.
Whether outlier filtering or exclusion was applied before normalization of assay responses in this processing step.

Process-level confidence or QC score indicating how well the response normalization performed on the raw assay data; typically a numeric score in the 0-1 or 0-100 range, record the value used in this workflow.

normalized_response.reasoning: The normalized_response node is a Derivative, so I included only computed assay outcomes derived from the processing step: normalized inhibition/activation values, toxicity indicators, active concentration summaries, response curves, and derivative-level confidence/status. I excluded raw assay artifacts and normalization procedure parameters because those belong to the Signal and Process nodes respectively. I also avoided previously generated collision-prone field names such as signal_to_noise_ratio, acquisition_date, storage_condition, and interpretation_confidence_score. The schema is limited to the final normalized metrics needed for downstream potency and toxicity analysis.

md_schema.descr: Normalized biological activity response for the compound after assay response processing, expressed as percent relative to the chosen controls; typical range -100 to 200 percent, e.g. 75.4.
Normalized toxicity or adverse-response metric derived from the assay response data, expressed as percent relative to controls; typical range -100 to 200 percent, e.g. 12.8.

Derived concentration associated with a normalized response threshold or effect level, reported in the assay's working concentration units; record the numeric value emitted by the workflow, e.g. 0.25.
Units associated with the derived concentration value for the normalized response metric; choose the concentration unit used in the assay output, e.g. uM, nM, or mg_per_l.
Compact summary of the normalized response curve derived from the assay data, including any fitted trend or notable nonlinearity; store the computed summary rather than raw plate values.
Overall status of the derivative call indicating whether the normalized response metrics are confident, partial, ambiguous, or rejected.

Overall confidence in the normalized response derivative, reflecting how robustly the raw assay data support the computed activity and toxicity metrics; typically a numeric score in the 0-1 or 0-100 range, record the value produced by the derivative step.
Free-text notes on the derived normalized response result, including any caveats such as saturation, baseline drift correction, or insufficient replicate support.

selectivity_analysis.reasoning: The selectivity_analysis node is a Process, so I included only the joint computational analysis parameters that integrate upstream derivatives: software identity, version, repository, input linkage, scoring strategy, weighting, and a process-level confidence/QC indicator. I excluded raw spectral and assay artifacts because those belong to the Signal nodes, and I excluded final potency/selectivity/candidate outputs because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided previously generated collision-prone field names, especially acquisition_date, storage_condition, signal_to_noise_ratio, and interpretation_confidence_score. The schema focuses on how the upstream evidence was combined to produce candidate-evaluation metrics.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software, pipeline, or computational workflow used to integrate NMR identity, MS properties, and normalized bioactivity into selectivity estimates; record the exact tool name used in this process.
Version of the selectivity analysis software or pipeline used for this process step; capture the exact release string, commit hash, or build number when available.
Source repository, package registry, or vendor distribution from which the selectivity analysis workflow was obtained; record the canonical code or source path when available.
Identifier of the NMR-derived identity features supplied as input to this analysis process; use the exact upstream derivative identifier for traceability.
Identifier of the MS-derived property features supplied as input to this analysis process; use the exact upstream derivative identifier for traceability.
Identifier of the normalized bioactivity metrics supplied as input to this analysis process; use the exact upstream derivative identifier for traceability.

Weighting scheme used to combine structural evidence and bioactivity metrics when estimating selectivity and potency; describe whether equal weighting, evidence-based weighting, or custom weighting was applied.
Method used to compute the selectivity estimate, such as ratio-based scoring, composite ranking, or multi-criteria decision analysis.
Threshold or cutoff applied during selectivity analysis to classify whether a compound meets candidate-suitability criteria; record the numeric threshold used by the workflow.

Process-level confidence or QC score indicating how well the integrated analysis combined upstream evidence into candidate-evaluation estimates; typically a numeric score in the 0-1 or 0-100 range, record the value produced by this workflow.

candidate_metrics.reasoning: The candidate_metrics node is a Derivative, so I included only the final computed evaluation outputs for each herbicide candidate: potency, selectivity, toxicity, ranking/decision status, and a summary confidence flag. I excluded upstream evidence, processing details, and raw signal properties because those belong to the Process, Capture, and Signal nodes. I also avoided previously generated collision-prone fields, especially acquisition_date, storage_condition, signal_to_noise_ratio, and interpretation_confidence_score. The schema captures the final integrated decision-support metrics a downstream user would need to rank candidates for agricultural use.

md_schema.descr: Internal identifier of the herbicide candidate for which the integrated evaluation metrics were computed; use the same stable compound identifier used across the workflow, e.g. 'PUR_001' or an equivalent unique label.

Computed potency score summarizing the herbicide candidate's effectiveness across the integrated analysis, derived from upstream structural and bioactivity evidence; record the final numeric score emitted by the workflow.

Computed selectivity score for the herbicide candidate, reflecting how specifically the compound acts against intended plant targets relative to off-target effects; record the final numeric score emitted by the workflow.

Computed toxicity or off-target risk score for the herbicide candidate, derived from the integrated analysis; higher values typically indicate greater potential toxicity, but follow the workflow's scoring convention.

Rank assigned to the candidate within the evaluated set after integration of potency, selectivity, and toxicity metrics; use an integer where 1 indicates best-ranked unless the workflow specifies otherwise.
Final decision or suitability label assigned to the candidate after integrated evaluation.
Concise textual summary of the integrated candidate evaluation, including the key reasons the compound was ranked as it was and any notable trade-offs between potency, selectivity, and toxicity.

Overall confidence in the final integrated candidate metrics, reflecting robustness of the combined structural and bioactivity evidence used to score the candidate; typically a numeric score in the 0-1 or 0-100 range, record the value produced by the derivative step.
